name: Peba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct; only Castelnau 1851 and other 19th-c. wordlists per Glottolog; no phonological description

sources.citation: Peña, Jaime G. 2009. A historical reconstruction of the Peba-Yaguan linguistic family. MA thesis, University of Oregon. Sec. 3.3 'Documentation on Peba' pp. 82-83; sec. 4.2.2 'Peba' pp. 94-95; fn. 13 p. 20; p. 103.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on Peba stress. States the Peba corpus is only Castelnau 1851 (~100 words) and Erben 1948 (21 words); 'There has not been any kind of phonemic analysis for Peba in the past' (p. 94); gives a grapheme-based segment inventory only. Fn. 13: accent marks in later chapters mean stress not tone 'since tone is not represented in the Peba or Yameo sources'; the stress interpretation of accent marks is applied to Yameo (p. 103), never to Peba.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1963. Documents et vocabulaires inédits de langues et de dialectes sud-américains. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 52: 7-60 (reprints Erben's Peba words).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Accessible republication of Erben's Peba items; would confirm whether any accent marking exists in that list. Not expected to contain a stress statement.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul. 1911. La famille linguistique Peba. Journal de la Société des Américanistes de Paris n.s. 8: 173-206.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative classification built on Castelnau/Marcoy/Orton vocabularies ('Les langues Peba et Yagua nous sont connues par des vocabulaires', p. 174); no remark on accent anywhere in the article (searched accent/tonique/phonét).

sources.citation: Castelnau, Francis de. 1851. Expédition dans les parties centrales de l'Amérique du Sud.. Histoire du voyage, tome 5. Paris: P. Bertrand. Appendice 'Vocabulaires des langues indiennes', XXIIe vocabulaire 'Langue des Pébas (Amazone)', pp. 296-297.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. A bare ~100-item French-orthography wordlist (Yuna, Riesé, Larcé, Capalé, Malayeré, Wasanou..); the acute accents are French spelling of vowel quality [e], there is no note on accentuation or pronunciation. This is the entire primary Peba corpus apart from 21 words in Erben 1948.

sources.citation: Erben, J. 1948. Po stopách dobyvatelů, proroků a svatých (travel account through the Amazon; 21 Peba words, used by Loukotka 1963). Prague.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only other primary Peba data besides Castelnau; Peña reports it holds just 21 words with no glossary, so it almost certainly says nothing about stress — listed only for completeness of the Peba corpus.
